findings.title: website_name bypasses TL0 untrusted-field filtering and is always serialized
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializer only consults `include_<attribute>?` predicates. The new guard is named `include_website_name` (without the question mark), and `website_name` is not added to `untrusted_attributes`. Consequently every user JSON now contains `website_name`, even for a TL0 user viewed anonymously, for whom the existing `website` attribute is intentionally suppressed by `untrusted_attributes :website`. The profile template then renders that field, leaking the host/path of a website that was deliberately hidden. Rename the guard to `include_website_name?` and apply at least the same `scope.restrict_user_fields?`/presence gate as `website`, or add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`.

findings.title: Host comparison treats unrelated hosts under public suffixes as the same domain
findings.body: The equal-label branch strips only the first label before comparing hosts. For an instance host such as `other.co.uk` and a user website of `example.co.uk`, both have three labels and both reduce to `co.uk`, so the code treats them as the same domain and returns `example.co.uk/path`. These are unrelated registrable domains (the same problem occurs for `alice.github.io` versus `bob.github.io`). The path should only be appended when the hosts actually belong to the same registrable domain, which requires public-suffix-aware comparison or a narrower exact/parent check rather than comparing `split('.')[1..-1]`.
